title: See the Taj Mahal at sunrise
description: Twenty-two years and twenty thousand workers for one man's wife. The marble changes colour through the morning, which is the reason to be early.

title: Walk the red sandstone of Agra Fort
description: Where Shah Jahan was imprisoned by his son and spent eight years looking downriver at the tomb he had built.

title: Watch the Ganga Aarti at Varanasi
description: Fire, brass lamps and bells at dusk on the river, in one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities on earth.

title: Take a rowing boat along the ghats at dawn
description: Eighty-four ghats along the west bank, with bathing, laundry, cremation and prayer all happening within a few hundred metres.

title: Climb to Amber Fort above Jaipur
description: A hilltop fort of mirrored halls and stepped courtyards. Walk up rather than taking an elephant.

title: Look over the blue city from Mehrangarh
description: One of the largest forts in India on a 120-metre cliff, with the indigo-washed old town spread out beneath it.

title: Sleep in the dunes outside Jaisalmer
description: A living fort of yellow sandstone at the edge of the Thar, with camel treks out to the dunes for the night.

title: Row on Lake Pichola at Udaipur
description: Palaces on islands, hills behind, and the whole city built to be looked at from the water.

title: Find the stepwells of Bundi
description: Fifty ornate stepwells in a small blue town, almost none of them visited, and a palace Kipling wrote about.

title: Walk Old Delhi from the Jama Masjid
description: The largest mosque in India, then down into Chandni Chowk, which is the most concentrated street in the country.

title: See the Qutb Minar and the iron pillar
description: A 73-metre victory tower from 1193, beside an iron pillar sixteen centuries old that has never rusted.

title: Eat in the langar at the Golden Temple
description: A hundred thousand people are fed free every day by volunteers. Cover your head, remove your shoes, and take a turn washing up.

title: Drive over the Khardung La
description: One of the highest motorable passes in the world at over 5,300 metres. Acclimatise in Leh for two days before you attempt it.

title: Camp beside Pangong Tso
description: A saltwater lake at 4,350 metres that changes colour hour by hour and runs sixty per cent into Tibet.

title: Cross the Spiti valley
description: A cold desert of thousand-year-old monasteries between the Himalaya and Tibet, on roads that wash out most summers.

title: Raft the Ganges at Rishikesh
description: Grade three and four water where the river leaves the mountains, in the town the Beatles made famous in 1968.

title: Walk the Valley of Flowers in monsoon
description: Three hundred alpine species flowering at once, only during the rains, seventeen kilometres up from the road head.

title: Sleep on a Kerala backwater houseboat
description: Converted rice barges on nine hundred kilometres of lagoon and canal. The smaller canoes reach the channels the boats cannot.

title: Walk the tea estates at Munnar
description: Hills carpeted in tea to the horizon, and once every twelve years the neelakurinji flowers turn them blue. Next in 2030.

title: Watch the Chinese fishing nets at Fort Kochi
description: Cantilevered shore nets worked by teams of four, brought here by traders from Kublai Khan's court.

title: See the gopurams at Meenakshi Temple
description: Fourteen gate towers covered in thirty-three thousand painted figures, in a temple complex the size of a small town.

title: See the rock-cut caves at Ajanta and Ellora
description: Thirty-four temples cut down into solid basalt at Ellora, and Buddhist paintings at Ajanta lost in the jungle until 1819.

title: Walk to a living root bridge in Meghalaya
description: Bridges grown from rubber fig roots over decades by Khasi villagers, reached by three and a half thousand steps down.

title: Look for tigers at Bandhavgarh
description: One of the highest densities of Bengal tigers anywhere. Book the core zone and go on consecutive mornings.

title: Find the quiet beaches in south Goa
description: The north is developed; the south still has palm-backed crescents with fishing boats on them.

title: Walk the Kathmandu durbar squares
description: Three royal squares of pagoda temples across the valley, much of it rebuilt since the 2015 earthquake.

title: Walk the kora at Boudhanath
description: One of the largest stupas in the world, circled clockwise at dusk by Tibetan pilgrims turning the prayer wheels.

title: Trek to Annapurna Base Camp
description: Ten to twelve days into a glacial amphitheatre ringed by seven-thousanders, sleeping in teahouses the whole way.

title: Trek to Everest Base Camp
description: Twelve days up the Khumbu to 5,364 metres. The flight into Lukla is the part people talk about afterwards.

title: Paraglide over Phewa Lake at Pokhara
description: Thermals off the Sarangkot ridge with the Annapurnas behind, and one of the best places in the world to learn.

title: Look for rhinos in Chitwan
description: Greater one-horned rhino, gharial and occasionally tiger, in grassland and sal forest on the Indian border.

title: Climb to the Tiger's Nest
description: A monastery on a cliff ledge nine hundred metres above the valley, reached by a steep two-hour walk each way.

title: Watch a masked cham dance at a tsechu
description: Days of masked religious dance in a courtyard, attended by the whole town in their best kira and gho.

title: Walk the Bumthang valley temples
description: The spiritual heart of Bhutan, with the country's oldest temples and a daily fee that keeps visitor numbers low.

title: Climb Sigiriya rock at first light
description: Twelve hundred steps up a granite plug to a fifth-century palace, past frescoes and a gateway of giant lion's paws.

title: See the Temple of the Tooth at Kandy
description: A relic of the Buddha kept in a gold casket, shown only during the evening puja. The August perahera is the big one.

title: Ride the train from Kandy to Ella
description: Seven hours through tea country on a British-built line, with the doors open and everyone hanging out of them.

title: Climb Adam's Peak overnight
description: Five thousand steps by torchlight to a footprint claimed by four religions, and a shadow the mountain casts at sunrise.

title: Look for leopards at Yala
description: The highest density of leopards in the world, in scrub jungle where they sleep on the rocks in plain view.

title: Watch blue whales off Mirissa
description: The continental shelf comes close to shore here, so the largest animal that has ever lived passes within a few kilometres.

title: Walk the ramparts of Galle Fort at sunset
description: A Dutch colonial fort on a headland, still lived in, with the sea on three sides and cricket on the green.

title: Snorkel a house reef in the Maldives
description: Twenty-six atolls of coral rings. A resort with a good house reef gives you more time in the water than any boat trip.

title: Swim with manta rays at Hanifaru Bay
description: Currents funnel plankton into a small bay and up to two hundred mantas come to feed. Snorkelling only, and numbers are capped.

title: Stay on a local island rather than a resort
description: Guesthouses on inhabited islands have been legal since 2009, and cost a fraction of a resort. Local rules on dress apply.

title: Take a boat into the Sundarbans
description: The largest mangrove forest on earth, shared with India, and home to tigers that swim between the islands.

title: Walk the longest beach in the world
description: One hundred and twenty kilometres of unbroken sand on the Bay of Bengal, and almost entirely domestic tourism.

title: Walk the tea gardens at Srimangal
description: Bangladesh's tea capital, where they serve a seven-layer tea that stays separated in the glass.

title: See the Hunza valley in autumn
description: Apricot and poplar turning gold under seven-thousand-metre peaks, on the Karakoram Highway near the Chinese border.

title: Walk to Fairy Meadows below Nanga Parbat
description: A grass shelf facing the eight-thousand-metre Rupal face, reached by a jeep road with a reputation and then a walk.

title: See the Badshahi Mosque and Lahore Fort
description: Mughal building at its height, with a mosque courtyard that holds a hundred thousand people, facing the fort across a square.

title: Walk an unrestored stretch of the Great Wall
description: Jinshanling and Gubeikou are steep, crumbling and nearly empty, which Badaling is not.

title: Cross the Forbidden City north to south
description: Nine hundred and eighty buildings over seventy-two hectares. Tickets are capped daily and sold online with a passport number.

title: Walk the Temple of Heaven park in the morning
description: The park fills at seven with tai chi, ballroom dancing, choirs and card games. The temple is the excuse.

title: Stand in front of the Terracotta Army
description: Eight thousand figures, each with a different face, found by farmers digging a well in 1974. Pit one first, then three.

title: Cycle the Xi'an city wall
description: Fourteen kilometres of Ming wall, complete all the way round, wide enough to ride four abreast.

title: See giant pandas at Chengdu
description: Arrive at opening; pandas are active in the cool of the morning and asleep by ten.

title: Walk the blue lakes of Jiuzhaigou
description: Travertine-dammed lakes so clear you can count the fallen trunks on the bottom, ringed by autumn forest.

title: Walk Tiger Leaping Gorge
description: Two days along a high trail above the Jinsha river, between two mountains over five thousand metres.

title: See the Yuanyang rice terraces flooded
description: Thirteen hundred years of Hani terracing, at its best when flooded in winter and reflecting the sky.

title: Walk the sandstone pillars at Zhangjiajie
description: Three thousand quartz sandstone columns in the mist, and the glass bridge over the Grand Canyon nearby if you can face it.

title: Cycle the karst country around Yangshuo
description: The limestone towers on the back of the twenty yuan note, best seen from a bike on the Yulong river road.

title: See the Mogao caves at Dunhuang
description: Four hundred and ninety-two painted grottoes on the Silk Road, a thousand years of Buddhist art sealed up until 1900.

title: Walk the Bund at night
description: Colonial banking houses on one side of the river and the Pudong skyline on the other, floodlit until eleven.

title: Walk Bukchon Hanok Village
description: Six hundred years of tiled-roof houses between two palaces, still lived in, so keep your voice down.

title: Watch the changing of the guard at Gyeongbokgung
description: Entry is free if you wear hanbok, which you can hire on the street outside, and most people do.

title: Eat at Gwangjang night market
description: Mung bean pancakes and raw beef tartare at counters that have been in the same families for generations.

title: Look into North Korea from the DMZ
description: The Joint Security Area opens and closes with the political weather. Book a licensed tour; independent access is not possible.

title: Cycle the royal tombs of Gyeongju
description: A thousand years of Silla capital, described as a museum without walls, with grass burial mounds in the middle of town.

title: Climb Hallasan on Jeju
description: South Korea's highest peak at 1,947 metres, a shield volcano with a crater lake, on an island of lava tubes and haenyeo divers.

title: Ride to the top of Taipei 101
description: The fastest lift in the world when it opened, and a 660-tonne steel damper ball you can walk around near the top.

title: Walk Jiufen old street in the rain
description: A gold-mining town of red lanterns and tea houses on a steep hillside above the sea. Better wet and out of season.

title: Walk the marble gorge at Taroko
description: Nineteen kilometres of marble canyon cut by the Liwu river. Check for closures; typhoons and quakes shut trails regularly.

title: Cycle the East Rift Valley
description: A hundred and eighty kilometres between two mountain ranges, through rice and indigenous villages on Taiwan's quiet side.

title: Ride the Alishan forest railway to the sunrise
description: A narrow-gauge line built by the Japanese for cypress logging, now climbing through three climate zones to a sea of cloud.

title: Ride the Star Ferry across the harbour
description: Running since 1888 and still the cheapest and best way to see the skyline. Sit on the lower deck.

title: Walk the Dragon's Back ridge
description: Forty minutes from Central to a ridge trail over the south coast. Three quarters of Hong Kong is countryside.

title: Eat dim sum from a trolley
description: Old-style tea houses where you flag down the trolley and stamp your own card. Go before eleven and share a table.

title: Take the tram to Victoria Peak early
description: The Peak Tram has run since 1888. The free circular walk around the summit is better than the paid viewing deck.

title: Walk from the ruins of St Paul's to Senado Square
description: A Portuguese church facade standing alone after an 1835 fire, and a world heritage old town behind it.

title: Eat a Macanese egg tart and pork chop bun
description: Four centuries of Portuguese and Cantonese cooking crossed into a cuisine that exists nowhere else.

title: See the Gandan monastery in Ulaanbaatar
description: A twenty-six metre gold Buddha rebuilt in 1996, in the one monastery Stalin's purges left standing.

title: Stay in a ger with a herding family
description: The valley where Genghis Khan's capital stood. Staying with herders is the normal way to travel here, not a novelty.

title: Ride a camel over the Khongoryn Els
description: Singing sand dunes up to three hundred metres high in the Gobi, near the cliffs where the first dinosaur eggs were found.

title: See the eagle hunters of Bayan-Olgii
description: Kazakh hunters flying golden eagles from horseback in the far west, with a festival each October.

title: Skate at Medeu above Almaty
description: The highest Olympic-size ice rink in the world at 1,691 metres, where dozens of world records were set.

title: Walk the Charyn canyon
description: Eighty kilometres of red rock canyon, often compared to Arizona, three hours from Almaty on the Chinese border road.

title: See Lake Kaindy's sunken forest
description: Spruce trunks standing dead and upright out of a lake formed by a 1911 earthquake, preserved by the cold water.

title: Stand in the Registan at Samarkand
description: Three madrasas facing a square, tiled in blue, and the single most impressive thing on the Silk Road.

title: Walk the Shah-i-Zinda avenue of tombs
description: A narrow street of eleven mausoleums, each tiled differently, built over eight centuries.

title: Walk the old town of Bukhara
description: A working Silk Road city rather than a monument: trading domes, a minaret Genghis Khan spared, and a pool in the centre.

title: Sleep inside the walls of Khiva
description: A walled desert town preserved almost whole, small enough to walk around the ramparts in an hour.
